title: Optimal radius for a two-point law
statement: Let $(\\Omega,\\mu)$ be a probability space, let $X:\\Omega\\to\\mathbb R$ be measurable, and suppose $q>2$, $0<\\lambda<1/2$, and $0\\le\\rho<1$. Assume $\\mu(X=1-\\lambda)=\\lambda$ and $\\mu(X=-\\lambda)=1-\\lambda$. Set $u=\\log((1-\\lambda)/\\lambda)$ and $\\rho_*=\\sqrt{\\sinh(u/q)/\\sinh(u/(q/(q-1)))}$. Then the inequality $\\|a+\\rho bX\\|_q\\le\\|a+bX\\|_2$ holds for all real $a,b$ if and only if $\\rho\\le\\rho_*$; likewise, $\\|a+\\rho bX\\|_2\\le\\|a+bX\\|_{q/(q-1)}$ holds for all real $a,b$ if and only if $\\rho\\le\\rho_*$.
replaced: Let $q>2$, $0<\lambda<1/2$, and $0\le\rho<1$. Let measurable $X$ on a probability space satisfy $\Pr[X=1-\lambda]=\lambda$ and $\Pr[X=-\lambda]=1-\lambda$. Then $H_{2,q,\rho}(X)$ holds if and only if $\rho\le\rho_*(q,\lambda)$, and the same equivalence holds for $H_{q/(q-1),2,\rho}(X)$. Here $\rho_*(q,\lambda)=\sqrt{\sinh(\ell/q)/\sinh(\ell/(q/(q-1)))}$ with $\ell=\log((1-\lambda)/\lambda)$. Write $H_{p,q,\rho}(X)$ for $1\le p\le q\le\infty$, $0\le\rho<1$, $X\in L^q(\mu)$, and $\|a+\rho bX\|_q\le\|a+bX\|_p$ for all $a,b\in\bbr$.
